Replacing corporate W-2 benefits as an independent UX consultant requires building your own safety net and tax-advantaged accounts across four primary pillars:

### 1. Retirement and wealth accumulation
- **Solo 401(k) over standard IRAs** — A Solo 401(k) allows contributions in two roles: an employee elective deferral up to **$24,500** for 2026, plus an employer profit-sharing contribution of up to **20% of net self-employment income** (capped at **$72,000** total across both sides). This substantially exceeds the $7,500 annual limit of your Traditional IRA.
- **Triple-tax-advantaged HSA** — Because you maintain an individual marketplace plan, pairing an eligible HDHP with your existing **Fidelity HSA** allows you to contribute up to **$4,400** (2026 self-only limit) with 100% tax-deductible contributions, tax-free growth, and tax-free qualified medical withdrawals.

### 2. Healthcare and tax treatment
- **Self-Employed Health Insurance Deduction (SEHID)** — 100% of your health, dental, and vision insurance premiums qualify as an above-the-line deduction on Schedule 1 (Form 1040). While this reduces your Adjusted Gross Income and federal income tax, note that it does not reduce your Schedule SE self-employment tax base (15.3%).
- **ACA Premium Tax Credit coordination** — When purchasing through the Health Insurance Marketplace, pre-tax contributions to a Traditional Solo 401(k) or HSA lower your Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI), which can increase your eligibility for premium subsidies.

### 3. Income protection and liability
- **Individual own-occupation disability insurance** — Without employer-provided short- or long-term disability, an injury or illness directly stops your consulting income. An individual policy with an "own-occupation" definition protects your ability to earn as a UX designer/consultant specifically, rather than any general job.
- **Cash flow buffer as self-insurance** — An emergency reserve of 6 to 9 months of personal expenses bridges both variable client invoice cycles and the standard 90-day elimination waiting period on long-term disability policies.
- **Professional liability (E&O)** — Unlike general liability, Errors & Omissions coverage protects against claims of project delays, design errors, or missed deliverable specifications in consulting contracts.

### 4. Low-admin cash flow automation
- **Automated tax withholding sweeps** — Maintain your current habit of routing a fixed percentage (e.g., 25–30%) of every incoming client invoice directly into your dedicated tax reserve before transferring operating cash to checking.
- **Quarterly safe harbor payments** — Pay federal estimated taxes using the prior-year safe harbor method (100% of prior-year tax liability, or 110% if prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000) to eliminate penalty risk without requiring complex monthly recalculations.
